1.1: These the words of the Preacher. Son of David. King in Jerusalem.
1.2: "Vanity of vanities," he said. "Ain't nothin' but smoke. All of it—just smoke."
1.3: What's the real gain from all this grindin'? All this sweat under the sun?
1.4: Generations come and go. Folks die. Babies get born. But the earth? She just keep spinnin'.
1.5: The sun rises, then drops. Then hurries right back to do the same thing again.
1.6: The wind do laps—south, then north, then around again. Spinnin' on repeat.
1.7: All the rivers pour into the sea, But the sea never fills up. The water goes back, starts over, and does it again.
1.8: Everything is exhaustin'. We don't even got words for it all. The eye ain't never satisfied with what it sees. The ear always tryna hear somethin' new.
1.9: What's been done? Gon' be done again. Ain't nothin' new under the sun.
1.10: You might think, "This brand new right here!" But nah—it already happened before, long before us.
1.11: And we don't even remember what went down back then. And the folks who come after us? They won't remember us either.
1.12: I was king in Jerusalem—yeah, me.
1.13: I made it my mission to learn it all. To figure out this whole life thing. But truth is? God gave humans a burden— We out here chasin' answers, but it's heavy.
1.14: I seen all kinds of work go down under the sun. And honestly? It's all chasin' the wind. Pointless.
1.15: What's bent can't be straightened. And what's missin'? You can't even count it.
1.16: I told myself, "Look how much I've accomplished. Look how wise I've become— Wiser than anybody before me in this city." I studied it all. Knowledge. Deep thoughts.
1.17: Then I said, "Let me get into madness too. Foolishness. Wild stuff." Guess what? Same thing. Wind chasing.
1.18: The more you know, the more it hurts. Knowledge bring grief. Wisdom don't always heal—it cuts.

2.1: I told myself, "Let's try joy. Let's chase pleasure. Let's see what that do." But honestly? That was pointless too.
2.2: I laughed at laughter. I looked at pleasure and said, "What it really doing for me though?"
2.3: So I tested myself with wine. I still kept some wisdom, but I wanted to see what life felt like livin' loose. Tried to figure out what actually makes life worth it while I'm down here.
2.4: I built houses. I planted vineyards for myself.
2.5: I made gardens, orchards—had fruit trees everywhere.
2.6: I built my own irrigation systems. Pools to water all those trees I planted.
2.7: I got servants. Male and female. Even had kids born into my house.
2.8: I stacked silver, gold, and treasure from everywhere. Got choirs. Got bands. All the entertainment I could dream of.
2.9: I leveled up—higher than anybody before me in Jerusalem. And I still kept my wisdom.
2.10: Anything my eyes wanted? I took it. I never told my heart "no." I enjoyed the grind. That was my reward—just the work itself.
2.11: But when I stood back and looked at everything I built with my hands? It still felt like tryna catch the wind. Nothing really hit. No real profit under the sun.
2.12: So I started thinkin': "What's the point of being wise? Or being reckless?" Even the next king ain't gon' do nothin' new.
2.13: Yeah, wisdom better than foolishness—like light better than darkness.
2.14: A wise man sees ahead. A fool stumbles blind. But guess what? They both still die.
2.15: So I told myself, "If I'ma die just like a fool, what all this wisdom for?" This too? Pointless.
2.16: 'Cause nobody gon' remember either of us. Wise or fool—we all get forgotten eventually. Death don't care how smart you was.
2.17: I started hatin' life. All this work under the sun was heavy. It all felt like chasing air.
2.18: And I hated everything I worked for. Why? 'Cause I gotta leave it to the one who comes after me.
2.19: And who knows if he gon' be smart… or a fool? Either way, he gettin' everything I built. That's wild. That's vanity too.
2.20: I gave up. I felt hopeless about all the years I poured into this grind.
2.21: You could work smart, work hard, work wise… and still leave everything to somebody who ain't put in a second. That's not just pointless—that's foul.
2.22: What do we even get from all this labor? All this late-night stress?
2.23: 'Cause even after work, your heart don't rest. All your days heavy. That too? Pointless.
2.24: You know what's best? Eat. Drink. Enjoy the good that comes from your grind. That joy? That's a gift from God.
2.25: Who can enjoy anything more than me? (And I still couldn't without Him.)
2.26: God gives wisdom, knowledge, and joy to the one who walks right with Him. But the sinner? He just out here workin'… stackin'… just to hand it off to somebody who actually pleases God. That too? Smoke. Wind. Dust in the hands.

3.1: Everything got its time. There's a season for every single thing under heaven.
3.2: A time to be born, and a time to die. A time to plant, and a time to pull it up.
3.3: A time to take down, and a time to build back. A time to kill, and a time to heal.
3.4: A time to cry, and a time to laugh. A time to mourn, and a time to hit your two-step.
3.5: A time to throw things out, And a time to pick stuff up. A time to hug, And a time to keep your distance.
3.6: A time to chase after somethin', And a time to let it go. A time to hold on, And a time to toss it out.
3.7: A time to rip things apart, And a time to stitch it back up. A time to hush, And a time to speak your truth.
3.8: A time to love, and a time to hate. A time for war, and a time for peace.
3.9: So what we really gain from all this grind?
3.10: I've seen the weight God gave us—the work we carry under the sun.
3.11: But hear this: He made everything beautiful… in its own time. And He planted eternity in our hearts. But still—we can't fully grasp what He doin' from start to finish.
3.12: I know this much: Ain't nothin' better than to live with joy, And do right while you got breath.
3.13: Eat good. Drink good. Enjoy what your labor brings. That right there? That's God's gift to you.
3.14: Whatever God does? It lasts. Ain't nothin' you can add to it. Ain't nothin' you can take away. He do it so folks will respect Him.
3.15: What's happenin' now? Been happened before. What's comin'? Already came. God gon' pull receipts from the past too.
3.16: I looked at the courtrooms—supposed to be just. But wickedness was sittin' in the judgment seat. Same thing in the church—iniquity where righteousness should be.
3.17: But I told myself: God got His time. He gon' judge everybody—the good and the wicked. Time for all things. Time for all works.
3.18: And I realized, God lets us see ourselves real raw— Like we ain't all that different from animals.
3.19: 'Cause what happens to us? Happens to them too. We all breathe. We all die. Ain't no special advantage. All of it? Still vanity.
3.20: We all made from dust. And guess what? We all goin' back to it.
3.21: Who really knows what happens to the spirit of a man after he dies? Does it rise? And what about animals? Do they stay low? We don't know.
3.22: So I figured this: The best thing you can do is enjoy the work you do. That's your slice of the pie. 'Cause who knows what's gon' happen after you gone?

4.1: I looked around again and saw all the oppression under the sun. Saw the tears of the oppressed—but no comforter. The oppressors got the power, but the victims? No one to hold them, no one to hear them.
4.2: I said, "Honestly? The dead might be better off than the living."
4.3: But even better than both? The one who ain't even been born— Ain't had to witness all this evil go down.
4.4: I saw how folks work hard, get skill, build somethin'— and next thing? Their neighbor hatin'. All that? Just wind. Ain't no real fulfillment in that.
4.5: The fool just sits with folded arms— and ends up eatin' his own life away.
4.6: Better to have one handful and peace of mind than two handfuls with stress, noise, and empty hustle.
4.7: Then I looked again and saw more vanity under the sun.
4.8: A man grindin' alone. No son, no brother. Still workin' like he got somethin' to prove. He never stops to ask: "Who am I doin' this for?" No joy. No rest. Just accumulation. That's not just vanity—it's a tragedy.
4.9: Two are better than one—'cause they get more done together.
4.10: If one fall, the other can help 'em up. But if you fall alone? Ain't nobody reachin' for you.
4.11: If two lie down together, they stay warm. But one by himself? He gon' freeze.
4.12: One might get jumped. But two can fight back. And a three-strand cord? That don't break easy.
4.13: Better a broke but wise young man than a stubborn old king who won't take advice no more.
4.14: That young man might've been in jail, might've been broke, but now he wearin' the crown.
4.15: I saw everybody ridin' for the new prince. He the people's favorite.
4.16: Crowds cheered for him. Everybody was on his side. But years later? New folks showed up… and they ain't care about him either. That too? Just wind. Just vanity.

5.1: Step careful when you show up in God's house. Don't come in loud with performin'— Come close to listen. That's better than runnin' your mouth like a fool, 'cause fools don't even know they doin' wrong.
5.2: Don't speak too fast in God's face. Let your heart slow down before your mouth runs off. He in heaven. You on earth. So keep your words short and solid.
5.3: All that dreamin'? That comes from a lot of stress. But too many words? That's how fools sound.
5.4: If you make a vow to God—don't play with it. Don't stall. Don't lie. God don't get joy from fools. Do what you said you'd do.
5.5: It's better to not make a promise at all than to promise and not come through.
5.6: Don't let your mouth write a check your life can't cash. Don't try to blame the angel later and say, "My bad, I ain't mean it." Why make God mad and watch all your work fall apart?
5.7: Talk too much. Dream too much. That's just more vanity. What matters? Fear God.
5.8: If you see the poor bein' crushed and justice gettin' flipped in courtrooms— don't act shocked. There's always a higher-up watchin' the one below him, and even they get watched by somebody higher.
5.9: But still—at the end of the day, the whole system runs off the land. Even the king eat from the same harvest.
5.10: If you in love with silver, you'll never have enough. Same with riches— it'll never feel like plenty. That, too? Just more smoke.
5.11: When you got more, more folks show up tryin' to eat off you. So what do you really gain, besides lookin' at your stuff and keepin' score?
5.12: The one who works hard sleeps well— whether his belly full or not. But the rich man? He stay up at night, wrestlin' with his abundance.
5.13: I seen a hard truth under the sun: Wealth held too tight ends up hurtin' the one who hoards it.
5.14: Sometimes money vanish overnight— bad business, bad luck. And when he finally got a child? Ain't nothin' left to give.
5.15: You come in this world naked. You leavin' the same way. Can't take nothin' you earned with you.
5.16: That's the harsh part— you leave with nothin', just like you came. All that grindin'? What was it for? Just tryna catch wind.
5.17: Folks live like that—eatin' in the dark, full of sadness, sickness, and anger. That's all they got to show.
5.18: But here's what I have seen: It's good to eat, drink, and enjoy what your work gives you. Enjoy your portion. That's what God gave you.
5.19: If God blessed you with wealth and the power to enjoy it, take that joy in your labor— that's the real gift.
5.20: When you live like that? You ain't stuck tryna rewind your past. God keep your heart busy with joy.

6.1: I seen somethin' heavy under the sun. It's not rare either—it happens to folks all the time.
6.2: A man blessed with money, success, and respect— He got everything he could ever want. But God ain't give him the power to enjoy it. Some stranger end up eatin' off what he built. That's smoke. That's a cruel pain.
6.3: Say a man got a hundred kids and lives a long, long life— But his soul still ain't full, and nobody even buries him proper? I'm tellin' you… a stillborn baby got it better than him.
6.4: That baby came and left in silence. No spotlight. No pain. Just peace.
6.5: It never saw the sun, never knew struggle— and it got more rest than that man ever will.
6.6: Even if he lived two thousand years… If he never experienced goodness? What's the point? Ain't we all headed to the same ground?
6.7: All that work we do? Just to eat. But the soul? The soul stay hungry.
6.8: What does the wise man really gain over a fool? What edge does the poor man got— even if he know how to move smart through life?
6.9: Better to enjoy what's right in front of you than to keep chasin' fantasies you can't catch. That too? Just graspin' at wind.
6.10: We already been named. We humans. We dust. And we can't go up against the One who's bigger than all of us.
6.11: The more we talk, the more we chase, the more we want— the more empty it all feels. So what's the real benefit?
6.12: Who really knows what's good for us down here, livin' this short, shadowy life? And who can tell us what's comin' after we gone?

7.1: A good name hit harder than perfume. And honestly? The day you die can mean more than the day you was born.
7.2: It's better to go to a funeral than a party— 'cause that's where we all end up. The living? They need that reminder.
7.3: Sadness? It can grow you more than laughter ever will. Pain teaches.
7.4: A wise heart sits in the heaviness. Fools stay chasin' a good time, missin' the lesson.
7.5: Better to get checked by someone wise than be serenaded by fools.
7.6: That loud, empty laughter? It's like dry sticks poppin' in a fire—no substance. Just noise. That too? Vanity.
7.7: Oppression can mess with a wise man's mind. Bribes? They'll rot your heart from the inside.
7.8: The end of a thing? Usually better than the start. And patience? That's stronger than pride.
7.9: Don't be so quick to snap. Anger love to live in a fool's chest.
7.10: Don't sit around sayin', "Back in the day was better." That kind of talk don't come from wisdom.
7.11: Wisdom with money? Now that's power. Both protect you, but one'll feed your soul.
7.12: Money can guard your life. But wisdom? Wisdom gives it meaning.
7.13: Think about what God does— You can't straighten what He made crooked.
7.14: When life's good? Rejoice. But when it's hard? Pause and reflect. God made both seasons, so you'd remember you don't control the future.
7.15: I seen it all: Good people dying too soon, Wicked folks livin' long and loud. It don't always make sense.
7.16: Don't overdo it tryna be "holier-than-thou." You'll burn yourself out.
7.17: But don't wild out either— You'll wreck your life early actin' reckless.
7.18: Hold both truths. Fear God, and He'll help you walk the line.
7.19: Wisdom make one person stronger than a whole city council.
7.20: Ain't nobody perfect. Everybody got sin on them.
7.21: Don't get caught up in every little thing folks say— You might hear stuff that'll hurt you.
7.22: 'Cause let's be real… You done said some wild stuff too.
7.23: I tested all this by wisdom. Said I'd figure it all out. But truth? It was too deep.
7.24: That thing out there? Far off. Buried deep. Ain't nobody fully cracked the code.
7.25: I chased after it though. Tried to understand life, tried to see what's wise, what's foolish, and what's just plain crazy.
7.26: And I found this one thing: A woman whose heart was traps and chains— She more bitter than death. If you walk right with God, you'll avoid her. But if you wildin'? She'll snatch your soul.
7.27: "I kept tryin' to piece it all together," says the Preacher. "One piece at a time."
7.28: "But I still ain't found the full answer. Out of a thousand men, maybe one got it. But among women? I ain't found one yet."
7.29: What I do know? God made us upright. We the ones who ran off schemin'— Tryna rewrite the rules and outsmart the Creator.

8.1: Who got insight like the wise? Who really know how to break things down? Wisdom make your face light up. It soften that hard look life gave you.
8.2: I'm sayin' this: Obey the king's orders. You made a vow to God—honor that.
8.3: Don't storm out the room. And don't stand up for evil just 'cause you mad. That king? He gon' do what he wanna do.
8.4: When the king speak, his word carry weight. Ain't nobody gon' ask him, "What you think you doin'?"
8.5: If you obey, you stay safe. And a wise one knows when to move and how to move.
8.6: Every situation got a time and a way to handle it. But let's be real—life still be hard.
8.7: We don't know the future. We don't even know when it'll hit. Nobody got the date stamped.
8.8: You can't hold your breath in when death come. You can't call time-out when it's your moment. And evil? It won't save the ones already locked into it.
8.9: I seen all this play out. I been studyin' how people move under the sun. Sometimes one man rules over another, and all it bring? Is harm.
8.10: I seen wicked folks get buried, And yeah, they used to show up at the temple, but now? Nobody remembers 'em. That too? Just more smoke.
8.11: When people don't get punished quick, they get bold with their evil. They think they safe.
8.12: But even if a sinner gets away with it a hundred times, I still know this: It'll go well for those who fear God.
8.13: But the wicked? They won't last. Their days will blow by like shadows, 'cause they don't fear the One in charge.
8.14: I seen some real twisted stuff: Righteous folks suffer like they were wicked. And wicked folks livin' like they holy. That don't sit right. That's vanity too.
8.15: So I say this: Enjoy what you can. Eat, drink, laugh. That's the one thing that stay with you while you grind through this life God gave you.
8.16: I tried to understand it all. Tried to study every move under the sun. Stayed up late. No sleep. Just thinkin'.
8.17: But even with all that? I realized—man can't figure out what God doin'. You can work, research, analyze… You still won't catch it all. Even the wise? They try… but they still can't fully wrap their heads around His ways.

9.1: I sat with all this in my heart, tryin' to figure it out—righteous folks, wise folks, what they do—all of 'em still in God's hands. And truth is? You can't look at what's happenin' and know if God mad or pleased.
9.2: 'Cause the same stuff happen to everybody. Good folk, bad folk. Churchgoers, wild ones. Folks who honor vows and folks who break 'em. Same outcome.
9.3: That's what's wrong with this whole thing: Everybody end up the same. People wild out while they alive—hearts full of madness—then boom. They gone.
9.4: But as long as you breathin'? There's still hope. Better to be a live dog than a dead lion.
9.5: The livin' know they gon' die. But the dead? They don't know nothin'. They can't earn nothin'. Nobody remember 'em.
9.6: Their love, their hate, their envy—it all faded. Ain't no comin' back to fix nothin'. Their part in this life is done.
9.7: So go 'head. Eat your bread with joy. Drink your wine with a glad heart. God already checked off your name.
9.8: Dress like you got peace. Keep oil on your head—look like somebody who know joy.
9.9: Love your partner. Enjoy life with the one you love—even in this short, unpredictable life God gave you. That love? That's part of your reward. That joy? That's the return on your grind.
9.10: Whatever your hands find to do—do it with all you got. 'Cause once you dead? Ain't no more plans, no hustle, no wisdom, no nothin'. The grave don't take ambition.
9.11: I looked again and saw: The fastest don't always win the race. The strongest don't always win the fight. Smart folks don't always get paid. Skilled folks don't always get favor. 'Cause time and chance hit us all.
9.12: You don't know your time. Just like fish caught up in a net, or birds caught in a trap—people get snatched up too, with no warning.
9.13: I saw some next-level wisdom once—and it stuck with me.
9.14: Small city. Not many people. Big king came through, built up traps all around it.
9.15: But in that city? One poor wise man. And by his wisdom? He saved the whole place. But guess what? Nobody remembered him.
9.16: So yeah… wisdom better than strength. But the world? It don't listen to the poor man's wisdom. They ignore his voice.
9.17: But even so? The quiet words of the wise hit harder than loud talk from fools in power.
9.18: Wisdom beat weapons. But one reckless fool? He can mess up everything good.

10.1: Dead flies make expensive perfume stink. Same way, one foolish move can mess up a whole rep of wisdom and honor.
10.2: A wise man's heart? Steady and sure. A fool's? All over the place—left, reckless, wrong.
10.3: Even when a fool tryna walk straight, his lack of wisdom show. He broadcastin' his ignorance loud and proud.
10.4: If your boss blow up on you, don't dip too quick. Sometimes holdin' your post is the smartest way to cool a hothead.
10.5: I seen somethin' wild under the sun—A ruler out here makin bad calls.
10.6: Fools sittin' high up in honor, while folks with real sense be overlooked and underpaid.
10.7: I seen servants ridin' horses, while royalty was walkin' like peasants. Whole thing felt backward.
10.8: Dig a hole for somebody else? You might be the one that fall in it. Break through a wall carelessly? You might get bit by what's hidin' behind it.
10.9: Workin' hard got its risks too—stonework can cut you, wood split wrong can hurt you.
10.10: Try to chop with a dull axe? You gon' sweat more. But sharpen it—use wisdom—and you'll get more done with less effort.
10.11: If a snake bite before the charm gets spoken, the charmer ain't useful. Same goes for a big talker who ain't got timing.
10.12: Wise folks speak life and grace. Fools? They get swallowed by their own mouth.
10.13: They start talkin' nonsense, and by the end, it's full-blown madness.
10.14: Fools love to overtalk—Like they know what's comin' tomorrow. Nobody knows the future like that.
10.15: All that runnin' in circles? They wear themselves out. They so lost, they can't even find their way to the city.
10.16: Woe to a land when the king act like a lil boy, and the leaders stay feastin' too early in the day—drunk before noon.
10.17: But blessed is the land with a noble king, and leaders who eat at the right time—for strength, not for turnin' up.
10.18: Sit around too long? The house gon' fall apart. The roof gon' leak. Things decay when hands don't move.
10.19: Folks throw parties to laugh. Wine get folks loose. But money? Money talk.
10.20: Don't badmouth the king—even in your head. Don't trash the rich—even in your bedroom. 'Cause you never know who's listenin'… A bird might catch your words and carry your secret across the sky.

11.1: Go 'head and toss your bread out there—even on the waters. You might not see it today, but it'll come back to you later.
11.2: Don't hold back what you got. Share with seven—nah, go on and bless eight. You don't know what's comin' to shake the world next.
11.3: When the clouds heavy, they gon' pour. When a tree falls, it ain't gettin' back up. It is where it lands. That's just how life be.
11.4: If you sittin' around waitin' for perfect weather, you'll never plant nothin'. If you scared of clouds, you ain't never gon' harvest.
11.5: Just like you can't trace the wind or explain how bones form in a baby's womb, you ain't gon' figure out how God work. He run all this.
11.6: So plant your seed in the morning. Don't sit on your hands come nightfall. You don't know what gon' hit—this one might work, that one might work, or both might blow up big.
11.7: Light hit different. Sunshine on your face? That's joy.
11.8: And if you get to live long, enjoy them years, every one. But don't forget—dark days still comin'. And they last a while. All of this? Still just a vapor.
11.9: Young blood, enjoy your youth. Laugh, dance, love—do your thing. Follow your heart, chase what you see. But just know: God keep receipts. You gon' have to answer for all of it.
11.10: So don't let your heart get bitter, and don't let your flesh run wild. 'Cause childhood and youth? They quick. They gone before you know it.

12.1: Remember your Creator while you still got energy. Before them hard days hit, and the years roll in where you say, "I ain't feelin' this no more."
12.2: Before your light start dimmin'—sun, moon, and stars don't shine the same, and the clouds keep comin' even after the storm.
12.3: When your arms shake like old gateposts, and your legs ain't holdin' you up no more. When your teeth few and far between, and your eyes can't see through the window like they used to.
12.4: When your ears ain't sharp, and the music sound faded. When you up at dawn from the smallest noise, but not even your favorite song moves you.
12.5: When you scared of steps, and the street feel like danger. When your hair turn white like almond blossoms, your step light like a grasshopper, and you just ain't got that desire no more. 'Cause at that point? Man go to his eternal rest—and the mourners walk the streets behind him.
12.6: Remember Him before the silver cord snap, before the golden bowl fall and break, before the jar crack at the spring, and the pulley shatter at the well.
12.7: 'Cause the dust gon' return to the ground where it came from, and the spirit? She gon' float back to God, the One who gave her.
12.8: "Vanity of vanities," the Preacher says—"All of this? It's just vapor."
12.9: And just so you know—the Preacher ain't just deep, he was wise. He taught folks. Broke things down. Put truth in order, wrapped it in words that hit right.
12.10: He searched for the realest way to say things—and every line he dropped? It was solid. No fluff. Just facts.
12.11: Wise words poke you like a cattle prod—they sting so you move. And the ones who know? They build steady like nails from one good Shepherd.
12.12: And listen, my child—don't get caught tryna read every book or chase every scroll. You'll wear yourself out. Too much study don't guarantee peace.
12.13: So here it is: The conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God. Keep His commandments. That's the whole job. That's the assignment.
12.14: 'Cause God gon' bring every deed to the light—even the secret ones. Good or bad—He gon' see it through.
